evidence.note: The upstream kernel assigns one output element per CUDA thread, applies train/flip/random-offset branches, rotates crop coordinates, and bilinearly samples the source image without synchronization.
The fixed-SHA adapter preserves single-evaluation ownership and is registered at one logical block of the upstream BLOCK=512 geometry as the negative control.
The extraction is tied to Darknet commit f6afaabcdf85f77e7aff2ec55c020c0e297c77f9 with source, adapter, patch, public-domain license, and probe hashes.
The upstream host fixes BLOCK=512 and covers size with cuda_gridsize; shrinking a singleton logical block without reassignment would leave output elements uncomputed.
The derived kernel changes only output-index ownership to a grid-stride loop, retaining the same per-element crop and interpolation helper for logical blocks 32 through 512.

Each output remains independent and executes the same floating-point instruction sequence; the GPU probe requires byte-for-byte equality against the original kernel compiled with the same flags and run on the same device.
